output.title: Official Correspondence to Governor-General Willem Arnold Alting regarding VOC Affairs
output.abstract: Formal letter addressed to Governor-General Willem Arnold Alting of the Dutch East India Company in Batavia, directed to the Council of the Netherlands Indies. The document appears to be a duplicate dispatch concerning an English vessel, the Atlas, with references to correspondence and official communications. The fragmentary nature suggests this is a cover page or header section of a larger administrative document from VOC records.

output.title: Ceylon Financial Demands and Currency Management, 1785
output.abstract: VOC correspondence addressing financial requisitions from Ceylon and measures to manage monetary circulation. Discusses constraints on private credit negotiation due to limited local resources, introduction of paper currency, copper coinage expansion, and interest rate increases to 9%. Documents coordination between chambers (Rotterdam, Amsterdam, Caab) regarding fund distribution and requests for sovereign financial support to meet Ceylon's monetary needs for 1785.

output.title: VOC Resolution on Emergency Relief Measures and Commodity Distribution
output.abstract: This document records VOC deliberations on emergency measures undertaken to address severe financial difficulties. The text discusses dependency on sovereign resolution regarding the Company's petition, and authorizes Commissioners to distribute Indian and Cape goods among regional chambers (kameren) as soon as feasible. Instructions are issued to chambers to remit allocated funds to India or the Cape at the earliest opportunity, reflecting urgent logistical and financial coordination during a period of constraint.

output.title: Extract from Letter to Governor-General Batavia, November 1784
output.abstract: Extract from correspondence dated 18 November 1784 from an Amsterdam assembly to the Governor-General and Council of the Indies in Batavia. Reports on previous communications sent in May and August 1784. Describes complications with mail delivery: documents shipped via the company vessel Zwaluw from Cape of Good Hope were damaged and the ship forced to dock at Padang where it was deemed irreparable and sold. Consequently, letters and papers were rerouted overland through Spain to Amsterdam.

output.title: Bengal Rice Supply Contract and Sjankoosen Diving Rights, 1780-1784
output.abstract: VOC correspondence regarding a proposal to supply Ceylon with 800-1000 lasts of Bengal rice annually at 4 rixdollars per sack (150 lb), accepted June 1780. The Company assumed direct management of sjankoosen (pearl/shell diving) operations instead of leasing them. Discusses outstanding payments, involvement of merchant Blinne, and complications from the capture of Trincomalee by enemy forces during the Anglo-Dutch conflict.

output.title: Linen Cloth Pacht Settlement and Arrears, Colombo and Galle, 1781-1782
output.abstract: VOC administrative resolution concerning the linen cloth (lijwaad) pacht contract for Colombo, Galle, and Kalpettij. Documents a dispute resolution where a contractor claimed significant losses due to limited cloth imports during his lease period. The Company agreed to reduce payment from 16,080 rixdollars to 7,250.36¾ rixdollars based on verified receipts. The document also addresses accumulated arrears from previous pacht holders (1776-1780), attributing delays to over-reliance on contractors' assurances rather than enforcement measures.

output.title: VOC Resolution on Secretary Compensation and Outstanding Payments at Pale, 1782
output.abstract: VOC administrative correspondence addressing compensation for secretaries' widows at Pale following orders from April 1782. Documents discuss settlement of arrears from fiscal years 1775-1776, calculation of the twentieth-penny tax, and accountability for outstanding payments. Emphasizes negligence in delayed collection and directs officials to enforce compliance and determine liability for unpaid obligations.

output.title: Fortification Works at Trincomalee and Defense Inadequacies, 1782
output.abstract: VOC administrative correspondence evaluating fortification construction at Trincomalee under Knight Des Roijs. The document addresses concerns raised in secret missives (April and June 1782) regarding incomplete defensive works and inadequate land-side fortifications. It concludes that the fort's defense was conducted deficiently and structural preparations were insufficient when the position fell to enemy forces.

output.title: VOC Naval Operations and Ship Safety During Anglo-Dutch Conflict, 1781
output.abstract: This VOC administrative document discusses measures taken to protect Dutch frigates and their cargo during wartime hostilities with the English, circa December 1781. It references orders sent to Trincomalee (Ceylon) directing the dispatch of two chaloupes from Pale, contingent upon English frigates ceasing operations. The document evaluates whether timely precautions were implemented to prevent vessels from becoming enemy prizes, noting the preference for destroying ships rather than allowing English capture.

output.title: Investigation into Alleged Smuggling and the Death of Skipper Jansen
output.abstract: VOC administrative document examining accusations of smuggling involving Skipper Jansen and an English vessel in Paalsche Bay. The investigation was suspended following Jansen's death, preventing proper interrogation of the accused. The document discusses how suspicion-casting tactics were employed to deflect blame, and concludes that the Warehouse Master's involvement in the matter actually increased rather than mitigated charges against him.

output.title: Resolution of 11 October: Ship Movements and Pepper Procurement Operations
output.abstract: VOC resolution documenting cargo transfers and maritime operations in the East Indies. The ship Spaarenrijk unloaded goods from De Bodt at Pale on 20 November, proceeding to Koetsjim to acquire pepper and rice. Reports indicate the vessel subsequently departed Porca on 1 December for Ceylon. Marginalia note an expedition to Mallebaer and delayed arrival of an expected vessel from that region.

output.title: Reallocation of Ship Stavenisse to Amsterdam Chamber
output.abstract: VOC decision dated 24th of the month to redirect the ship Stavenisse from Zeeland Chamber to Amsterdam Chamber due to missed Ceylon voyage. The reallocation was necessary to secure adequate pepper and saltpeter supplies for loading two return ships. Paalse officials were instructed to prepare proper ballast for the vessel's new assignment.

output.title: Arrival and Cargo Distribution of VOC Ships Stavenisse and Middelwijk
output.abstract: Report documenting the arrival of the return ship Stavenisse at Batavia on 10 October, originally consigned to Zeeland chamber but reassigned to Amsterdam. Details cargo operations including rice, pepper, and provisions distributed to Batavia, Koetsjiem, and Gale. Also records the arrival of ship Middelwijk on 19 October with partial cargo discharge and subsequent redistribution. Includes administrative resolutions and disposition orders from November-December period.

output.title: Horse Inventory and Linen Trade Regulations at Colombo and Madras
output.abstract: VOC administrative record documenting horse populations on the island of Delft, including Persian stallions, indigenous horses, mares, and foals, with maintenance costs of ƒ817.5.8. Also records resolutions from March and April regarding revival of linen (lijwaaten) collection on the Madura coast, establishing price controls for coarse linens to encourage procurement of standard assortments for company trade.

output.title: Pearl Diving Operations in Ceylon and Tutucorijn: Contract Negotiations with the Count of Bijland
output.abstract: VOC administrative document concerning the management of pearl diving (sjankozen duikerij) operations along the Ceylon coast and at Tutucorijn. Records financial valuations (3600 rixdollars for Ceylon; 70 for Tutucorijn in August 1650) and discusses contractual obligations with the Count of Bijland regarding compensation for diving expeditions conducted on company account. Includes resolution from September 3rd addressing below-standard revenues and proposed payment arrangements.

output.title: VOC Administrative Records: Calpettah Duties, Pearl Banks Inspection, and Merchant Petitions
output.abstract: VOC administrative document recording fiscal and operational matters including duty assessments on calpettah goods, merchant payment rates (16.32 rixdollars versus standard 15.12), and inspection of pearl banks along Ceylon's Arippu coast. References decisions from October 22 and December 29, with involvement of officials including dessave De Bock and merchant Blinne's petition regarding 1786 duties.

output.title: Pearl Oyster Inspection Reports from Kalpettij and Madras Coast
output.abstract: VOC administrative report documenting inspection visits to pearl oyster banks at Kalpettij and the Madras coast, conducted by Captain Commandant and subordinate merchants. Despite high expectations, inspections yielded minimal and immature pearl oysters. The report references resolutions from December 29 and November 22, noting plans for further surveys of pearl banks along the Madura coast, with findings to be reported to the Directors.

output.title: Purchase of Trade Goods and Ship Provisions, 1710
output.abstract: VOC record documenting procurement of merchandise and supplies during the preceding year, including the emergency purchase of 6,000 sacks of Bengali rice from the English ship Stasting at six ropijen per sack (150 lb.), and Dutch maritime supplies such as rope, sailcloth, yarn, pitch, tar, and hemp acquired for the Dutch squadron's operational needs. References multiple resolution dates throughout 1710.

output.title: VOC Spice and Dutch Merchandise Inventory: Purchase and Sales Ledger
output.abstract: VOC accounting document recording inventory transactions for spices (nutmeg, mace, cloves, cinnamon) and Dutch merchandise including copper, silver, textiles, glassware, ammunition, and sailcloth. Lists quantities in pounds, purchase prices (Inkoops), sales prices (Verkoops), and profit margins in guilders. Demonstrates VOC's dual trade in Eastern spices and European goods, with detailed cost accounting and percentage calculations for profitability analysis.

output.title: VOC Cargo Manifest and Financial Account: Transport and Goods Inventory
output.abstract: This VOC accounting document records a comprehensive cargo manifest and financial ledger, detailing transported goods (Schenkagie Goederen) destined for Coromandel and other trading posts. Inventory includes textiles (pingams, cormandels), spices (pepper, cloves), provisions (rice, sugar, coffee, butter), medicines, and naval supplies. The document tracks purchase prices (Inkoops) and sales profits (verkoops winst) in Dutch guilders, with total values reaching approximately ƒ232,000. Multiple departmental entries (smithy, armory, carpentry, dispensary) indicate comprehensive VOC operational logistics.

output.title: VOC Council Resolutions on Spice Prices and Domain Revenues, 1784-1785
output.abstract: Council of India resolutions from July 1784 and June 1784 establishing commodity prices: nutmeg at 100 rixdollars per last and mace at 150 stuivers. Documents accounting discrepancies in clove sales calculations by negotie bookkeeper Rakel. Reports domain revenues for fiscal year 1785/6 at ƒ397,429.4, exceeding prior year by ƒ113,547.9.8. Addresses salt transport prohibition to uplands affecting Putelang lease auctions, with temporary monthly lease arrangements implemented.

output.title: VOC Domain Leases and Tax Farming Arrangements in Ceylon, 1990-992
output.abstract: VOC administrative record documenting the public leasing of company domains in Jaffna and Mannar on 26-27 August 1990, with textile and salt pan leases in Colombo, Gale, and Kalpettai valued at 20,000 rixdollars. Details preferential bidding rights granted to previous bidders and tax reductions (150 rixdollars) awarded to the Levais salt pan leaseholder and Jaffna cloth traders due to losses from salt transport prohibitions and passport regulations.

output.title: Pagoda Mint of Colombo: Gold Coinage Output, September 1784–August 1785
output.abstract: VOC administrative record documenting gold coinage production at the Pagoda Mint in Colombo over a twelve-month period. The mint produced 101,759 pagodas from 79,092 marks of fine gold. The document details shipment routes via the Cape of Good Hope and overland transport, with itemized listings of individual gold bars (bhaar goud) numbered 1–25, their weights in marks, and fineness ratings. Significant for understanding VOC monetary operations and precious metal management in the Indian Ocean trade network.

output.title: Gold Shipment Inventory from Batavia and Zeeland, VOC Transport Records
output.abstract: VOC accounting document recording detailed inventory of gold bars (bhaaren goud) and gold fragments received via ships Triton from Batavia and Stavenisse from Zeeland. Lists 54 gold bars with individual assay values in karats, weights, and prices. Entries numbered 1-43 document systematic cataloging of precious metal shipments with standardized valuations around 18-21 karats, typical of VOC precious metals management in the 18th century.

output.title: VOC Mint and Precious Metals Account: Gold, Silver, and Japanese Copper Assay Records
output.abstract: VOC financial accounting document detailing precious metals processing and coinage operations. Records multiple batches of gold assays, refined Japanese copper standardization to 18/24 karat, and three separate minting batches (mark trois) with fine silver calculations at ƒ375 per mark. Includes labor costs for silversmiths, munters, smelters, and administrative personnel, with detailed weight measurements in ounces and grains. Entries reference fiscal oversight and transfer to main treasury (groote geld kassa).

output.title: VOC Mint Operations and Silver Coinage Accounts, Batavia
output.abstract: Financial accounting document detailing the Batavia mint's (Fanuiis Munterij) coinage operations across multiple minting cycles. Records calculations of silver marks, fineness assessments, and monetary valuations in guilders and pagodas. Documents the processing of worn silver items from government stores and their reminting, with references to administrative resolutions from April and November. Includes transport accounts and profit calculations from gold and silver coinage operations.

output.title: Commission for Colombo Fortification Works Assessment
output.abstract: VOC administrative document regarding a commission appointed March 3rd to evaluate fortification works at Colombo, modeled on the Galle assessment. Major Paravicini's assignment to Trincomalee delayed completion of the survey. The document discusses the status of fortification improvements needed and anticipates the ship Stavenisse may require additional days before departure due to extensive squadron work in Galle Bay, with a preliminary report expected to follow.

output.title: Fortification Maintenance Directives and Lieutenant Lawe's Accountability
output.abstract: VOC administrative document outlining protocols for maintaining three fortifications through continuous labor and resource allocation. Lieutenant Lawe, serving as engineer, must submit annual oaths regarding faithful treatment of coolies, laborers, and craftsmen under his department. Strict penalties are threatened for any dereliction of duty, with no leniency permitted. The document emphasizes systematic progress toward achieving defensive readiness of the fortified positions.

output.title: Petition for Lieutenant Lowe's Salary and Carpentry Expenses Account
output.abstract: A VOC administrative document petitioning for an annual salary increase of 1800 rixdollars (150 rixdollars monthly) for Lieutenant Lowe, arguing that fair compensation enables employees to fulfill their duties faithfully. The petition emphasizes that modest wages prevent servants from resorting to unauthorized means. Attached is a detailed accounting of carpentry and repair expenses totaling ƒ64,822:5:8 across multiple locations including Colombo, Jaffnapatnam, Mannar, and Galle.

output.title: VOC Administrative Audits and Pharmacy Records, 1784
output.abstract: VOC administrative document detailing quarterly pharmacy reports and confrontatie (audits) of workshops and warehouses at Colombo and Jaffnapatnam conducted in August 1784. Records approval of administrative procedures, verification of iron magazine inventories, ammunition house accounts, and material warehouse dispositions, with references to resolutions from March through December documenting compliance with VOC orders and accounting procedures.

output.title: VOC Account Settlements and Agent Dispositions: Tranquebar and Colombo, 1784-1785
output.abstract: Administrative record documenting VOC resolutions regarding financial accounts and personnel matters. Details disposition of agent Geeke's accounts, warehouse inventory findings at Pale (August 1784), and agent Peeke's dismissal from Tranquebar (January 1785) for final accounting. References discrepancies between Peeke's and Captain Lieutenant De Bellon's records on the Coromandel coast, with Peeke summoned to Colombo for resolution.

output.title: General Expenses and Profits: VOC Financial Statement 1784/5
output.abstract: Financial accounting document comparing VOC general expenses and profits for fiscal year 1784/5 against previous year 1783/4. Records profits of ƒ643,770 (Dutch currency) versus ƒ329,829 previously, and expenses of ƒ1,503,564 versus ƒ744,562, showing increased expenditures. Includes audit reports of payroll books from Colombo, Jaffnapatnam, and Palo, and inventory valuations of cash, merchandise, provisions, and military equipment totaling ƒ6,126,694.

output.title: Requisition of Supplies and Accounting Procedures for Nagapatnam and Colombo
output.abstract: VOC administrative document detailing requisitions for supplies and provisions across colonial stations. References accounting procedures for Nagapatnam and Colombo, including provisional accounting entries for transferred bookkeepers and medical personnel. Cites multiple resolutions from 1747 (February through May) governing payment specifications and approval of minor expenditure items. Emphasizes compliance with established VOC protocols for supply requisitioning and financial documentation.

output.title: VOC Commodity Inventory and Provisions List, January 1786
output.abstract: A detailed VOC warehouse inventory documenting spice commodities, textiles, provisions, and military supplies. Lists quantities in pounds and pieces of powdered sugar, bandij, mace, nutmeg, cloves, Japanese copper, tin, pewter, porcelain dishes, nanking linen, rice, wax candles, arrak, Persian red earth, flints, and copper nails. Includes allocations for the dispensary, armory, and trade warehouse. Dated January 1786 with numerical notations indicating valuations or transaction records.

output.title: VOC Supply Requisitions: Timber Works, Pharmacy, and Smithy Stores
output.abstract: VOC inventory requisition document detailing supplies for three workshops: the timber yard (Timmerwerven), pharmacy (Medicijn winkel), and smithy/coopers shop (Smits en Kuijpers Winkel). Lists medicinal substances including radix China, lignum Sassafras, and various oils; timber specifications for ship construction with precise measurements; and hardware materials including Venetian borax and iron stock. Contains quantities in pounds and pieces with five-year comparative data, indicating systematic provisioning records for colonial operations.

output.title: Annual Supply Requisition and Cash Inventory by Residency (1782)
output.abstract: VOC inventory document detailing annual supply requirements and cash reserves across multiple residencies in Ceylon and the Coromandel Coast, including Colombo, Jaffna, Mannar, Galle, Matara, Trincomalee, Batticaloa, and Kalpattinam. Lists timber materials (large and small planks, beams) allocated to shipyards and carpentry workshops, with corresponding financial accounts in guilders and quantities of rice and provisions measured in lasts.

output.title: Justice Council Complaint Against Orphan Masters and Enforcement Powers
output.abstract: This document records a formal complaint by the Justice Council (Raad van Justitie) regarding orphan masters (weesmeesters) who failed to comply with council directives. The Governor-General clarifies that orphan chambers must submit to the Justice Council's authority and that enforcement measures (contrainte) may be applied against non-compliance. A resolution from September 3rd establishes the legal framework for execution of such orders without exception.

output.title: VOC Educational Institution: Quality of Instructors and Student Performance
output.abstract: This document discusses resolutions from April 15 and September 6 regarding a VOC-sponsored educational establishment. The writer expresses concern about the quality of instructors available locally, arguing that better-qualified teachers are necessary given the Company's substantial financial investment. The text notes that recent graduates sent to the Netherlands had to enter lower classes, suggesting inadequate preparation. It concludes that meaningful educational outcomes can only be achieved through improved instructor selection, as recommended by the scholarship committee.

output.title: Jaffena Orphan Masters' Petition for Widow and Orphan Support
output.abstract: The Orphan Masters (Weesmeesteren) of Jaffena petitioned to provide maintenance for European widows and orphans using surplus interest from their chamber funds, which accumulated to 1117 rixdollars by August 1784. The VOC approved this proposal on May 7th, commending their charitable oversight. Distributions would be made from future interest earnings without diminishing the principal capital, ensuring sustainable support for destitute dependents.

output.title: Diaconate Capital and Leper House Fund Accounts, Colombo 1759
output.abstract: Financial statement documenting the Diaconate capital totaling ƒ126,161:14:6¼ distributed across VOC settlements: Colombo, Jaffna, Mannaar, Gale, Mature, and Kalpettij. Records repairs to the Leper House (Leproosen huijs) costing ƒ1,709:14:½ and the Leper Fund balance of ƒ31,735:17½ as of August. Includes accounting resolutions and fund management documentation from September 1759.

output.title: Pearl Fishery Disputes with Tuticorin: Nabab's Commissioners and Doctor Dot's Mission
output.abstract: VOC correspondence regarding pearl fishery conflicts with Tuticorin and the Nabab. Documents commissioners sent by the Nabab to oversee pearl bank inspections, and the arrival of English Doctor Dot as mediator for negotiations between the Nabab and the Company. References resolutions from September-December and pending reports on diplomatic outcomes.

output.title: Renewal and Issuance of Don and Modliaar Titles at Jaffna, 1760
output.abstract: VOC administrative directive regarding the renewal and issuance of honorary titles (Don and Modliaar) at Jaffna. Holders since 1760 must renew certificates within six weeks at a cost of 12.5 rixdollars; new applicants may obtain titles for up to 25 rixdollars. The document clarifies that these titles pose no operational inconvenience to the Company and participation is voluntary, though strict regulations govern their use.

output.title: Appointment of Thomas Nagel as Landmeeter in Jaffnapatnam
output.abstract: VOC document commending Thomas Nagel, artillery lieutenant and sworn landmeeter in Jaffnapatnam, for his instrumental role in bringing local territories under direct Company control and suppressing a dangerous mutiny. Nagel's sixteen years of service as landmeeter provided extensive knowledge of the land and its inhabitants, making him the suitable candidate to govern the Wannische Lands effectively.

output.title: Negotiations with French Governor Coutancheau at Pondicherry for Supply of Goods
output.abstract: Correspondence regarding VOC negotiations with French Governor Coutancheau at Pondicherry to obtain needed supplies and ammunition. The French governor expressed willingness to provide goods but declined to set prices, instead offering to deliver items against receipt (quitantie) with accounting to be settled between European governments. The VOC accepted this arrangement and received ammunition goods on French government receipt.

output.title: Discharge of Captain-Lieutenant Heupner as Armory Superintendent
output.abstract: Administrative record documenting the dismissal of Captain-Lieutenant Klaas Ditloff Heupner from his position as superintendent of the weapons chamber (wapenkamer) due to advancing age and declining health, while retaining his commission as artillery captain. The document references ammunition accounting matters submitted to the governing council and discusses personnel matters within the VOC military hierarchy.

output.title: Governance Crisis and Arrest: Tensions Between Colonial Authority and Dissent
output.abstract: This VOC document discusses escalating tensions between colonial officials and an arrested individual resisting governmental authority. The Governor, concerned about deteriorating relations between the Dutch Republic and the Emperor, takes action involving Colonel D'Hugonet. The text emphasizes the urgency of addressing the situation, warning that delay will produce serious consequences. A detailed report from the fiscal is referenced regarding the arrested person's resistance to government authority, submitted to the Zeeland Chamber directors.

output.title: Judicial Proceedings Against Regiment of Luxembourg and Disciplinary Concerns
output.abstract: VOC official correspondence addressing criminal proceedings against the Regiment of Luxembourg and its officers, initiated by the fiscal authority. The document discusses persistent disciplinary problems and conflicts between VOC administration and the regiment command, arguing that the current military structure poses risks to company interests. The matter is referred to the Heeren Bewindheberen (Board of Directors) of the Zeeland Chamber for final resolution regarding appropriate disciplinary measures.

output.title: VOC Ordinance on Luxembourg Regiment Supplies and Equipment Costs
output.abstract: VOC administrative document addressing the surplus distribution of five stuivers per guilder and provisions for the Luxembourg regiment's integration with Company troops. Details the supply of nankings, linens, and military equipment from Company warehouses at standard rates equivalent to Dutch military provisions. Establishes procedures for accounting weapon distributions to recruits lacking firearms, with annual settlement of repair costs and expenses charged to the regiment under Capitulation terms.

output.title: VOC Military Personnel Roster: Soldiers, Musketeers, and Sailors
output.abstract: A detailed muster roll documenting VOC military personnel including soldiers, musketeers, sailors (mattroosen), and a drummer. Lists 22 sailors, 6 musketeers, and additional soldiers with their names and places of origin across Europe and VOC territories. Includes references to detachments at Tinkonomale and Jaffanasche, indicating deployment across the Indian Ocean network. The roster reflects VOC's multinational recruitment practices in the early 18th century.
